task: I’m putting together a one-period digital literacy lesson pack for a middle-school class and want the pieces to feel like they belong together, not like I grabbed them randomly. Could you start on Slidesgo and pick one fun, classroom-appropriate presentation template that would work for a grade 7 or 8 lesson, ideally something bright and student-friendly rather than corporate, because I want to use that visual style as the theme for everything else? Open the actual template page and leave it open so I can see the preview images, and note whether it’s available for Google Slides or PowerPoint. Then use Google to find a printable worksheet or practice page for an 8th-grade student on basic marketing strategies or persuasion techniques, like identifying advertising tricks or persuasive techniques, and open the actual resource page so I can check that it really looks classroom-ready and printable. After that, go to Citation Machine and verify that Harvard style is actually available there by navigating to wherever the citation styles are shown or selectable, because I’ll need to cite the worksheet and any media correctly; leave that proof visible or keep the page open. Finally, on YouTube, find three beginner-friendly videos about online safety or cybersecurity basics that would make sense for students, open each video in its own tab so I can compare them, and play one of them briefly so you can tell me what the opening covers. At the end, send me a short lesson-pack summary with the Slidesgo template name and format option, the worksheet title and where it’s hosted, the evidence that Harvard style can be selected on the citation site, and the three YouTube video titles with their channel names.

### Middle School Digital Literacy Lesson Pack Summary

#### 1. Presentation Template (Slidesgo)
* **Template Name:** Technology Subject for Middle School: Digital Citizenship and Internet Safety Presentation
* **Format Availability:** Available for **both Google Slides and Microsoft PowerPoint** (as well as Canva).
* **Location / Open Tab:** **Tab 825319277** (`https://slidesgo.com/theme/technology-subject-for-middle-school-digital-citizenship-and-internet-safety`)

---

#### 2. Printable Marketing & Persuasion Worksheet
*(Note on Search Engine Access: Direct search queries on Google encountered an IP-level automated traffic block/reCAPTCHA. Following task rules, a bot-check attempt was made, after which DuckDuckGo was utilized to locate the live resource.)*
* **Worksheet Title:** Advertising Worksheet (Advertising and Persuasion)
* **Hosting Site:** BrightSprout (`worksheets.brightsprout.com` / `brightsprout.com`)
* **Classroom Readiness:** Fully formatted with printable options (Print, Download PDF, Answer Key, Ink Saver), featuring exercises on daily product analysis, advertisement design element identification, color emotion associations, slogan/logo analysis, identifying "calls to action," and vocabulary matching (Persuasion, Targeting, Call to Action, Emotions, etc.).
* **Location / Open Tab:** **Tab 825319278** (`https://worksheets.brightsprout.com/120707/advertising-worksheet`)

---

#### 3. Citation Machine Harvard Style Verification
* **Evidence:** Citation Machine supports Harvard referencing directly via its dedicated **Harvard Citation Generator** ("Free HARVARD Citation Generator and Format" with source citation tools such as "Cite a Website in Harvard"). The platform also explicitly lists Harvard alongside MLA, APA, and Chicago ("Generate citations for any assignment in thousands of styles, including MLA, APA, Chicago and Harvard").
* **Location / Open Tab:** **Tab 825319279** (`https://www.citationmachine.net/harvard`)

---

#### 4. YouTube Videos (Online Safety & Cybersecurity Basics)
Each video has been opened in its own dedicated tab:

1. **Video 1:**
   * **Title:** Safe Web Surfing: Top Tips for Kids and Teens Online
   * **Channel:** watchwellcast
   * **Location / Open Tab:** **Tab 825319280** (`https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yrln8nyVBLU`)
   * **Opening Coverage (Played):** The narrator opens with humor, noting that by "powers of deduction" there is a 100% chance the viewer uses the internet since they are watching on YouTube. The host welcomes the student to WellCast and introduces internet safety, playfully telling the viewer to hear them out before rolling their eyes and thinking their parents or teachers have already told them everything about online dangers.

2. **Video 2:**
   * **Title:** Being Safe on the Internet
   * **Channel:** AMAZE Org
   * **Location / Open Tab:** **Tab 825319281** (`https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HxySrSbSY7o`)

3. **Video 3:**
   * **Title:** Teaching Students the Basics of Online Security
   * **Channel:** Kaspersky
   * **Location / Open Tab:** **Tab 825319282** (`https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Mqo2yMvX8OY`)
